blockMcqs.question: What's the core difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler produces a separate artifact without running it
A compiler is faster than an interpreter, always
An interpreter produces machine code up front
A compiler only works on dynamically typed languages
blockMcqs.explanation: The interpreter executes directly as it goes, emitting no standalone artifact.

blockMcqs.question: Which stage of the pipeline catches a type or scope error?
options: Lexing
Parsing
Semantic analysis
Code generation
blockMcqs.explanation: Lexing and parsing only check words and structure; meaning rules come later.

blockMcqs.question: What does an AST encode that a flat token stream cannot?
options: The exact source whitespace
The target CPU's registers
The final machine instructions
Nesting and operator precedence
blockMcqs.explanation: Tree shape captures structure; a token list is just a flat sequence.

blockMcqs.question: What does a JIT do that pure AOT does not?
options: Compiles everything before the program runs
Skips building an AST entirely
Profiles the run and compiles only hot code
Avoids producing any native code
blockMcqs.explanation: AOT compiles all code up front, blind to which paths actually run hot.

blockMcqs.question: Why can't you keep data on the call stack past a function's return?
options: The garbage collector erases it eagerly
The frame is popped, so its memory is reclaimed
Stack memory is read-only after return
The calling convention forbids reads there
blockMcqs.explanation: Returning pops the frame, so a pointer to a local now points at freed space.

blockMcqs.question: On a stack-based VM, what does the ADD instruction do?
options: Adds two named registers and stores the result
Reads two memory addresses by index
Loads a constant onto the operand stack
Pops two operands and pushes their sum
blockMcqs.explanation: Stack VMs have no registers; operands live on the operand stack.

blockMcqs.question: When a JIT's speculation is later violated at runtime, it:
options: Crashes the program safely
Deoptimizes and falls back to the interpreter
Recompiles the whole program from scratch
Ignores the new type and keeps the fast code
blockMcqs.explanation: Falling back to the safe interpreter is what makes aggressive speculation safe.

blockMcqs.question: Which statement about typing is correct?
options: Strong typing is the same as static typing
Dynamic languages cannot be strongly typed
Static/dynamic is about when types are checked
Weak typing means types are checked at runtime
blockMcqs.explanation: Strong/weak is a separate axis about implicit conversions; Python is dynamic and strong.
